w:r.w:t: Managers build a 15-player Ligue 1 squad under a budget, set a weekly lineup, and score points from real match stats. Private leagues add a rivalry phase before the lineup deadline: a manager can lock a player, send a buy offer, or take a bench player from a rival. The overall ranking is the sum of match points. Influence is never added to it.
This document is the decision record for version 1. Rules are numbered so later edits can cite them. If two sentences disagree, the numbered rule wins and the other sentence must be corrected.
Sections 2 and 3 are the game. Build them as written.
Sections 4 to 6 say how a gameweek moves from an open squad to a published score.
Sections 7 to 9 say what to build, and in what order.
Section 10 lists the three choices that can still change without a new design.
The reader is the person implementing the game. The document names the product, the rules, the data, and the weekly jobs. It does not specify visual design, marketing, or a mobile client.
Accounts, a budget squad, weekly lineups, transfers, and four chips.
Points from finished matches, with a per-player breakdown.
An overall ranking and private leagues.
Lock, Offer, and Heist inside a private league.
Live points while a match is in progress. Scores update when a fixture is finished, and again if a stat is corrected.
Bonus points, weekly price changes, and a two-way player swap.
Cash prizes, draft leagues, and a public marketplace between strangers.
LFP logos, the competition logo, club crests, and player photographs, unless a license is purchased.
The base game is a full season on its own. Rivalry, in section 3, changes who owns a player. It does not add a second scoring system.
The version-1 season is 2026/27 Ligue 1: 18 clubs and 34 matchdays. Each matchday is one gameweek, numbered 1 to 34. The season opens on the weekend of 23 August 2026 and ends on matchday 34.
A manager owns exactly 15 players: 2 goalkeepers, 5 defenders, 5 midfielders, and 3 forwards.
The squad budget is €100.0 million. Money is stored as an integer count of €0.1 million, so 1000 means €100.0 million. A purchase that would make the remaining budget negative is rejected.
A squad holds at most 3 players from the same club. The club is the one on the player’s current stint for that gameweek.

An editor sets each price, in €0.1 million steps, before gameweek 1. Public market-value lists, including Transfermarkt, may inform that meeting. They are not imported by a job. A price changes only when the player moves between Ligue 1 clubs, and the new price is set before the next gameweek opens. Version 1 has no automatic weekly price change.

A player who leaves Ligue 1 is ineligible. If the manager has not sold that player before the next lineup deadline, the game sells the player at list price and leaves an empty slot. An empty slot scores 0. A lineup cannot be submitted while the squad has fewer than 15 eligible players.
The starting XI uses one of 4-4-2, 4-3-3, 3-5-2, 3-4-3, 5-3-2, 5-4-1, or 4-5-1. The other 4 players are the bench, in order 1 to 4. A starting goalkeeper can be replaced only by a goalkeeper.

The captain’s points are doubled, including a negative total. The vice-captain’s points are doubled only when the captain plays 0 minutes. Played means more than 0 minutes. Triple Captain sets the captain multiplier to 3 and leaves the vice-captain at 2.

The lineup deadline is the kickoff of the first fixture in the gameweek. Market transfers close at that same instant. The rivalry window closes 60 minutes earlier, as rule R6 states. Every deadline is stored in UTC and shown to managers in Europe/Paris.

Each gameweek includes 1 free transfer. Each further transfer in that gameweek costs −4 points on that gameweek’s score. A transfer is one sale and one purchase. Unused free transfers do not roll over. Before the gameweek 1 deadline, transfers are unlimited and free, and any unspent budget remains.
The sale price and the purchase price on the open market are the current list price.

A manager may play Wildcard, Free Hit, Bench Boost, and Triple Captain once across gameweeks 1–17, and once again across gameweeks 18–34. The chip sits on the lineup. It is consumed at the lineup deadline and can be removed before that deadline.
Unlimited transfers, and no points hit.
Unlimited transfers, and no points hit. Those transfers edit a temporary squad.
The temporary squad is discarded. The persistent squad remains, including any heist or accepted offer from that week.
All 15 players can score. Automatic substitutions do not run.
The captain multiplier is 3. The vice-captain is still doubled only if the captain plays 0 minutes.
Free Hit and the persistent squad.

Selecting Free Hit copies the persistent squad into a temporary squad. Transfers made while the chip is selected edit only the copy. Removing the chip before the deadline discards the copy. Rivalry resolution edits the persistent squad. If that removes a player who is still in the copy, the copy’s slot is emptied and must be filled before the lineup deadline.

They run only when Bench Boost is off. Once a starter’s fixture is finished or cancelled, a starter with 0 minutes is replaced by the first bench player who played more than 0 minutes and leaves a legal formation. The bench is tried in order. A postponed fixture is not finished, so that starter is not replaced yet.

A player scores only the events below. Appearance points use a single band: 0 minutes scores 0, 1–59 minutes scores 1, and 60 or more scores 2. The bands do not stack. Version 1 does not award bonus points.
Clean sheet, if 60 or more minutes
Goals conceded, per 2, if 60 or more minutes

Saves use integer division: 5 saves score 1 point, and 2 saves score 0. A penalty goal counts as a goal, and an assist on it still scores. An own goal does not create an assist. A clean sheet requires 60 or more minutes and 0 team goals in that match.
Version 1 uses the team’s full-match total. The deduction of 1 point per 2 goals applies only when the player played 60 or more minutes. It does not track the minute the player left the pitch.
A yellow card is −1. A red card is −3. Two yellow cards in the same match are stored as one red card and zero yellow cards, so the total is −3.

Automatic substitutions run first. Event points are totaled next. The captain multiplier is applied to that total. If the captain played 0 minutes, the captain scores 0 and the vice-captain is doubled when the vice-captain played more than 0 minutes. If both played 0 minutes, no multiplier is applied.

A postponed match stays in its original gameweek and scores when it is played. The gameweek is not final until every fixture is finished or cancelled. A cancelled fixture scores 0 for every player and is not moved.

A manager has one squad for the season. That squad’s match points count in the overall ranking and in every private league the manager has joined. Winning a heist does not add points. It can change which players are owned, and those players then score in every table.

Rivalry is the interactive layer. It is a structured exchange before the lineup locks: protect a player, agree a sale, or take an unlocked bench player if you can pay and the squad stays legal. Nothing is decided by a random roll.
Lock, Offer, and Heist exist only inside a private league. The overall ranking has none of these actions.
Any manager can create a private league and receives a join code of at least 8 random characters. The code is enough to join. A manager may belong to more than one private league.
Each league membership has its own Influence balance. Influence does not move between leagues, and it is not added to a score.
Every membership starts at 2 Influence, so a heist can be attempted before gameweek 1 has been scored.

When a gameweek becomes final, Influence is awarded from that private league’s gameweek points. Tied managers each receive the award of the shared rank, and the next distinct score receives the next rank’s award. Two managers tied for first both receive 3, and the following manager receives 2.
Every other manager with a legal lineup
The window closes 60 minutes before the lineup deadline. The game then resolves actions in the order in section 4. The manager has those 60 minutes to field a legal XI after a squad change.
During the window, members of that league can see each squad split into the saved starting XI and the bench. Captain, vice-captain, and the selected chip stay hidden until the lineup deadline.
In one league and one gameweek, a manager may play one Lock and one offensive action. The offensive action is either one Offer or one Heist, not both.

A Lock names one of the manager’s own players. It costs nothing and does not use the offensive action. A locked player cannot be taken by a heist that resolves that gameweek. A Lock does not stop an Offer the owner accepts. A manager may Lock a player and still play an offensive action.

An Offer names a rival’s player, a price at least equal to the list price, and one of the buyer’s own players of the same position to release to the market. The owner may accept, refuse, or counter with a higher price before the rivalry deadline. Refusal is free and final. A counter replaces the price; if the buyer does not accept it before the deadline, the Offer expires. On success, the buyer pays the agreed price, the owner receives that price, and the named player goes to the market at list price. The buyer’s budget must cover the agreed price minus the released player’s list price.

A Heist names a rival’s player, an Influence bid of at least 2, and one of the taker’s own players of the same position to release. The bid is reserved when the Heist is submitted. Success is entirely conditional. There is no die roll and no hidden chance.
A Heist succeeds at the rivalry deadline only when all of the following are true. If any one fails, the squad is unchanged and the reserved Influence is refunded.
The target is on the owner’s saved bench at the deadline.
That player was not taken by a successful heist in the previous gameweek.
The owner has not already lost a player this gameweek to an accepted Offer or a Heist.
The taker still owns the named release player.
After the swap, the budget is at least 0, no club has more than 3 players, and the position counts are still 2, 5, 5, and 3.
The bid is the winning bid against that squad. The higher bid wins. An equal bid loses to the earlier submission.

On success, the taker spends the reserved Influence. The taker’s budget changes by the released player’s list price minus the target’s list price. The owner receives the target’s list price. The released player returns to the market at list price. The taken player cannot be the target of a Heist in the next gameweek. An Offer for that player is still allowed.
A player who is in the saved starting XI at the rivalry deadline cannot be heisted. The owner can move the player into the XI before that deadline, and the pending Heist then fails.
A squad loses at most one player per gameweek. Accepted Offers are applied before Heists. If an Offer has already removed a player, every Heist against that squad fails.

If several Heists name the same player, only the winning bid is applied and the others are refunded. If they name different players in the same squad, only the single winning bid against that squad is applied.
A Heist or an accepted Offer changes the persistent squad. It is not undone when a Free Hit ends.

A manager cannot target a player they already own. An action against a player whose fixture has already kicked off is rejected. The rivalry window is not reopened after its deadline, including when a postponed match is later given a new kickoff.
These are the same rules as above, stated as outcomes an implementer can test.
The buyer cannot cover the price after the release.
The action fails. The squad is unchanged. A Heist refunds its Influence.
The swap would break the club limit or the position counts.
The action fails. The squad is unchanged.
The Heist fails and its Influence is refunded. An Offer can still be accepted by the owner.
The target is in the starting XI at the rivalry deadline.
The Heist fails and its Influence is refunded.
Two Heists name one player, or two Heists hit one squad.
The higher bid wins. The other Influence is refunded. A tie goes to the earlier submission.
The same player was heisted in the previous gameweek.
The new Heist fails and its Influence is refunded.
The owner refuses the Offer, or nobody answers it.
The taker no longer owns the player they promised to release.
The action fails. A Heist refunds its Influence.

Before gameweek 6, Sam has €2.0 million free and 4 Influence. Sam releases a bench midfielder listed at €5.5 million and bids 2 Influence for a rival’s unlocked bench midfielder listed at €7.0 million. The budget after the swap would be €2.0 + €5.5 − €7.0 = €0.5 million, and Sam would still be inside the three-player club limit. No higher bid targets that squad. The Heist succeeds. The rival receives €7.0 million. Sam has 2 Influence left. The taken player cannot be heisted in gameweek 7.

If, before the rivalry deadline, the rival moves that player into the starting XI, the Heist fails and Sam’s 2 Influence is refunded. Sam still has 60 minutes to set a lineup. The same refund happens if the rival used Lock on that player.
A gameweek is a timestamped state machine. The worker may run late. The deadline that counts is the stored timestamp, not the moment the job happens to start.
The previous lineup deadline has passed, or the season has opened.
Market transfers, lineup edits, Lock, Offer, and Heist.
No new rivalry actions. Offers and Heists for this week are resolved. Lineups and market transfers stay open.
The lineup is frozen, the chip is consumed, and transfer hits are charged. No sales.
The first finished fixture has stats.
Published points update as further fixtures finish. A postponed fixture contributes 0 until it is played.
Every fixture is finished or cancelled.
The breakdown is stable except for a stat correction. Influence for this gameweek is awarded.

At the rivalry deadline the worker does four things, in this order. It expires Offers and counters that were not accepted. It applies accepted Offers in the order they were accepted. It resolves Heists using rules R12 to R16. It refunds every failed or losing bid.
Points are computed only from PlayerMatchStat. A person does not type a total. The published total is the sum of the breakdown.

If a stat changes after publication, the worker recomputes every breakdown that used that fixture and replaces the total. The previous total is stored in an audit row. A heist is not undone. Influence awards are recomputed from the corrected ranks. A balance may become negative. A new bid is rejected when the balance cannot cover it. Influence already spent stays spent.

Lineups in the postponed gameweek stay locked. The next gameweek opens on its own dates. Influence for the postponed gameweek is awarded only when that gameweek becomes final. Until then, a starter whose only match is postponed is not automatically substituted.
A lineup that names a sold player.

If the saved lineup still names a player the manager no longer owns, the game keeps the saved formation, keeps the starters who are still owned, and fills holes from the bench in bench order. Any slot that still cannot be filled scores 0.

Names below are the names to use in the database and the API. Money columns are integers of €0.1 million. A clean sheet is not stored: it is 60 or more minutes and zero goals conceded in that fixture.
The 2026/27 competition: 34 gameweeks and its date range.
A Ligue 1 club for this season.
One row per club per season.
Identity and position: goalkeeper, defender, midfielder, or forward.
Which club the player belongs to, from which gameweek, and at what list price.
No overlapping stints for one player.
Home club, away club, kickoff, matchday, and status.
One fixture per match. Status is scheduled, live, finished, postponed, or cancelled.
Minutes and the scoring events for one player in one fixture.
One row per player per fixture.
Number 1–34, rivalry deadline, lineup deadline, and phase.
One row per season and number.
The persistent 15, the remaining budget, and the season.
One squad per user per season.
A player on that squad, the price paid, and how they were acquired: initial, market, offer, or heist.
One row per squad and player. At most 3 share a club.
Formation, captain, vice-captain, chip, and submission time for one gameweek.
One lineup per user per gameweek.
Starting or bench, and bench order 1–4.
Eleven starters and four bench players.
Market sale and purchase, the gameweek, and any −4 hit.
Hits are rows, not a handwritten total.
Which chip was consumed in which half and gameweek.
One use of each chip per user per half.
Private league name, owner, and join code.
One membership per user per league.
Award, reserve, spend, refund, or correction, with a signed amount.
Append-only. The balance is the sum.
Lock, Offer, or Heist: actor, target, release player, bid or price, status, and time.
At most one Lock and one offensive action per user, league, and gameweek.
The manager’s total for one gameweek, and whether it is final.
One score per user per gameweek.
One player’s events, base total, and multiplier.
The score total equals the sum of its lines, plus transfer hits.
The previous total, the reason, and the time of a correction.
Written only when a published total changes.
Fields that the rules depend on

stores player, fixture, minutes, goals, assists, goals conceded, saves, penalties saved, penalties missed, yellow cards, red cards, and own goals. Ingest normalizes two yellow cards in one match to zero yellow cards and one red card before scoring reads the row.

stores the league, the gameweek, the actor, the type, the target player, the release player when there is one, the Influence bid when it is a Heist, the offered price when it is an Offer, the status, and the
creation time. Status is submitted, accepted, countered, refused, expired, succeeded, or failed. The creation time is the tie-break in rule R12.

stores enough of the breakdown to explain the total on screen: minutes band, goals, assists, clean sheet, goals conceded, saves, penalty events, cards, own goals, the base total, and the multiplier. A manager can see why a player scored what they scored without reading the raw stat row.
The worker owns this pipeline. A web request may read the latest published rows. It does not compute an official total.

On a schedule, the worker pulls fixtures and player match stats for the current gameweeks from one stats provider and upserts Fixture and PlayerMatchStat. It also normalizes cards, as section 5 requires.
At the rivalry deadline, the worker runs the resolution order in rule T1, writes InfluenceLedger rows, and refuses any later action for that gameweek.
At the lineup deadline, the worker stores the lineup that was valid at that timestamp, consumes the chip, and writes transfer-hit rows.
For each locked lineup, the worker applies automatic substitutions, the points table, and the captain multiplier. A starter whose fixture is still postponed is left in place and scores 0 for now.
The worker writes GameweekScore and one GameweekScoreLine per contributing slot. League tables and the overall table read these rows and add nothing else.

When a stat changes, the worker repeats scoring and publication for the affected fixtures, writes ScoreAudit, and recomputes Influence if the gameweek is final. Running scoring twice on the same stats produces the same rows.

Ingest runs every 10 minutes from the first kickoff of a gameweek until every fixture that weekend is finished or postponed, and once more the next morning to catch corrections. A postponed fixture is polled again when its rescheduled kickoff is known.
Auth, squad commands, lineup commands, league commands, and reads of gameweeks and scores.
Ingest, rivalry resolution, lineup lock, scoring, and corrections. It is a separate process from the web server.
The entities in section 5. Deadlines, prices, points, and Influence are integers or timestamps, not strings.
Version 1 is one API and one database. A cache, a queue, or a second region is not required. The worker can poll the database for deadlines that have passed.

One paid stats API supplies Ligue 1 fixtures and per-player match stats. The first ingest adapter targets API-Football. Sportmonks is the replacement if that coverage is missing events the points table needs. The rest of the system talks to the adapter, not to the vendor’s field names. Provider fixture identifiers are stored on Fixture so updates match the same match.
Transfermarkt is a manual reference for spellings and for the meeting that sets initial prices. Version 1 does not scrape it, and it is not the source of goals, assists, cards, or minutes.

Club and player names are stored as text because the game cannot be played without them. The product does not ship LFP logos, the competition logo, club crests, or player photographs unless a license for those assets is purchased.

An account is an email and a password. The password is stored only as a slow hash. The session cookie is httpOnly. A private-league join code is the secret that admits a manager to that league, so codes are random and at least 8 characters.
Properties the build has to keep
Official points can be recomputed from PlayerMatchStat and the locked lineup.
Scoring and rivalry resolution are idempotent.
A failed Heist never changes the squad and always returns the reserved Influence.
Each screen talks to the API with the commands below. Reads are safe to repeat. Commands that change a squad, a lineup, or a rivalry action are rejected when the relevant deadline has passed.
Create an account or sign in.
See the next deadline and season points.
Filter the list by club, position, and price.
Read the 15 players, the budget, and the club counts.
Sell one player and buy one.
Set the formation, XI, bench order, captain, vice-captain, and chip.
Create a league, join with a code, and read the table.
Lock, offer, counter, accept, refuse, or heist.
Read the gameweek total and each player’s breakdown.

The rivalry screen is available only inside a private league, and only while that gameweek is open. It shows the caller’s Influence, their pending action, and each rival’s saved XI and bench. It does not show captains or chips.

Each slice is playable on its own. Rivalry is last because it needs a legal squad, a locked lineup, and a league already in place. Do not start slice 5 by stubbing a random chance of success. The Heist rules are deterministic.
Clubs, players, prices, and fixtures for 2026/27, with a read-only browser.
Accounts, the initial 15, market transfers, and a lineup with a deadline.
Full-time scoring, the breakdown screen, postponed matches, and stat corrections.
The overall table and private leagues with a join code. Standings are match points only.
Influence, the rivalry window, Lock, Offer, and Heist, including the failure cases in section 3.
Live points, bonus points, weekly price changes, and two-way swaps.

The numbered rules are enough to build version 1. The three items below are the ones a later edit is expected to revisit. Until that edit, the rules cited here are in force. Change the cited rule. Do not leave a second answer in a comment or in this section.

Rules R4, R5, and R11 set a starting balance of 2, awards of 3 / 2 / 1 / 1 / 0, and a minimum bid of 2. If play shows that heists are too rare or too common, change those numbers only. Do not add a random roll to tune how often a Heist succeeds.

An Offer in version 1 is cash for a player. The buyer releases a same-position player to the market, not to the seller. A swap in which two managers exchange players is not allowed. Adding it would be a new action, with its own deadline and failure cases.
Rule B12 splits the season after gameweek 17, the halfway point of 34 matchdays. Move that boundary only if the published Ligue 1 calendar no longer has 34 matchdays.
Document version 0.1. The next edit should bump the version on the cover and say, in one line at the top of this section, which rule numbers changed.
